paper_id: Lu et al. - 2008 - Pseudo Trust Zero-Knowledge Authentication in Anonymous P2Ps
title: Pseudo Trust: Zero-Knowledge Authentication in Anonymous P2Ps
venue: IEEE Transactions on Parallel and Distributed Systems
motivation: Identity-based trust models conflict with user anonymity in P2P systems, creating an unresolved trade-off.
problem_framing: How to authenticate peers without exposing real identities while maintaining trust management?
key_insight: Generate unforgeable pseudonyms via one-way hash; use ZKP so parties authenticate without revealing secrets.
method_signature: ZKP-based mutual authentication with pseudo identity certificates (PIC) generated from quadratic residues.
evaluation_criteria: Impersonation success probability bound by 2^-k; latency overhead within acceptable bounds per simulations and prototype.
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: PT response time ~7x overt Gnutella due to onion paths; PIC generation costs ~8 seconds on popular PCs (one-time).
evidence_for_taste: R always accepts the PI of peer I as valid
computationally infeasible to find an x
extra traffic cost also slightly fluctuates
growth of P2P overlay has little impact
thinking_moves: Define the trade-off explicitly, then search for a cryptographic primitive that decouples identity from trust value
Replace centralized CA with mathematical intractability assumptions (factoring, square roots modulo n)
Bound impersonation probability formally via soundness lemma, then show adversary must break factoring
Layer zero-knowledge proof atop existing anonymous routing (APFS) rather than redesigning anonymity from scratch
Verify completeness first (honest parties always succeed), then prove soundness (cheaters detected with overwhelming probability)
